current_bottleneck: 287b showed that the local-history coordinate is still viable and that normalized change replay is the right support primitive. The remaining miss is now in the retrieval key: a single mixed embedding appears to overweight fast local change alignment and underpreserve the slow structure needed for local cointegration robustness and active-cell mean reversion.
last_result_summary: Iteration 111 ran 287b-v0 and got 3/11. It materially improved change KS, level KS, jump realism, and mean-reversion aggregate profile versus 287a, but still failed local cointegration robustness and active-cell MR support. Iteration 112 then selected 287c-v0 as the next follow-up: keep the 287b support primitive fixed and split the retrieval key into fast and slow channels.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 287c-v0 as a two-timescale local-history retrieval backbone that encodes fast normalized changes and slow cumulative displacement separately while keeping the 287b support primitive fixed.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
